play_name: Notice if they show up before you give more
behavioral_target: Chasing people who don't show up, or passing over people who do.
trigger: You feel pulled toward someone who is hard to reach.
old_play: You chase people who don't show up, or skip people who do.
function_of_old_play: This keeps the chase going, but you don't learn if they'll show up for you.
new_play: Notice how much the other person shows up — do they text back, keep plans, and treat you well? Give more only as they show more.
what_to_expect: You find out sooner if someone can really meet you back — or can't.
why_supports_task: It uses what people actually do as your proof, so your choice is based on facts.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Chasing unavailable people; dating unavailable people; brushing off available people.
context_limitations: You still get to feel drawn to someone. This isn't about dating people you don't like.
review_reason: Some sources have unclear function; consolidation spans selection + pursuit.

play_name: Check a worry before you decide
behavioral_target: Pushing past a warning sign or a gut feeling.
trigger: Something early on worries you, or your gut says something is off.
old_play: When something feels off, you push the feeling away or stay anyway.
function_of_old_play: This keeps things going and skips a hard talk or a hard choice.
new_play: When something worries you, name exactly what you saw. Then watch it or ask about it before you get more serious.
what_to_expect: Some worries turn out to be nothing. Others turn out to be real. Either way, you learn the truth.
why_supports_task: You use your own eyes and gut as real facts again.
supporting_competencies: Conflict Management → Objectivity, Reflection; Trust → Congruence
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Ignoring red flags; ignoring intuition; staying after seeing red flags.
context_limitations: If a worry is about your safety, don't test it — get to a safe place.

play_name: Give another chance only if things really change
behavioral_target: Giving open-ended chances or staying past your own judgment.
trigger: Someone lets you down, and you're deciding whether to keep going.
old_play: You give another chance, or stay longer, even when nothing is changing.
function_of_old_play: This keeps the relationship going for now.
new_play: If you give another chance, name one real change you need to see, and by when. Then look at what actually happened.
what_to_expect: You see if the change is real or just hoped for.
why_supports_task: It turns open-ended hope into a choice based on what you see.
maintaining_behaviors_consolidated: Staying too long; giving one more chance.
context_limitations: Fixing things and just waiting are not the same. This depends on whether the other person owns their part and changes.
